newsitem.title: USA: IBM's CEO 1996 salary at $1.5 million.
newsitem.headline: IBM's CEO 1996 salary at $1.5 million.

text.p: Louis Gerstner, chairman and chief executive officer of International Business Machines Corp was paid a salary of $1.5 million for 1996 and received $3.27 million in bonuses, according to a proxy filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

In 1996, IBM granted Gerstner a stock option covering 300,000 shares of IBM common stock. This grant has a longer vesting period than typical IBM stock options, the filing said. There is no vesting for the first three years (until 1999) and then the options vest over four years (ending 2002).

The company said it made the award to encourage Gerstner to stay at IBM for an extended period of time. The grant was based on the chairman's continued contributions to IBM's financial performance, his effective leadership of a complex business in a very dynamic and competitve industries and analyses of stock option awards to CEOs at other major firms.
IBM said the strike price for these stock options is $126.69 a share for all options that expire February 26, 2006.
In 1995, Gerstner's base salary in 1995 was $2.0 million and his bonus was $2.75 million.
IBM's chief financial officer, G. Richard Thoman, received a base salary of $556,250 in 1996 and a bonus of $625,000.

John M. Thompson, an IBM senior vice president who heads its software business, earned $556,250 in 1996 and a bonus of $603,000. Ned Lautenbach, senior vice president, earned $561,250 and a bonus of $571,000. Robert Stephenson, another senior vice president, earned $472,500 and bonus of $543,000.

Gerstner entered into an employment agreement with IBM on March 26, 1993 and it was amended in January 1996 to provide that Gerstner earned a payout from the 1994-96 Long-Term Performance Incentive based on IBM's cumulative financial results over the three years valued at $2,072,567.
One half of the amount was paid in cash and the balance was delivered in stock units that are restricted for two additional years, IBM said in the filing.
At the end of 1996, Gerstner held 29,289 performance stock units, 65,000 restricted stock units and 6,696 shares of restricted stock having a combined value of $15,248,735.
IBM plans to hold its annual meeting in Dallas on Tuesday, April 29.
